entries.tell: A violet or indigo accent that no token in the system owns.
entries.instead: Name a palette of four to six colours with a role each, and take the accent from it.

entries.tell: Glows, halos and blurred gradient blobs behind content.
entries.instead: Build depth from the system's elevation steps, and let one shadow token carry it.

entries.tell: Headings or metrics painted with a gradient fill.
entries.instead: Set text in one solid colour from the palette and let size and weight carry the emphasis.

entries.tell: A warm cream page surface with a terracotta accent, chosen by reflex.
entries.instead: Derive the surface from the brand or the subject, and record the choice and its reason in the palette.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: Hex, rgb or hsl colours and pixel sizes written straight into component styles.
entries.instead: Reference the colour, spacing and radius tokens, and propose a token to the design system steward when none fits.

entries.tell: Text on a surface that falls below the contrast the pair needs.
entries.instead: Pick the text and surface tokens as a pair, and list the pair in the contrast pairs file in both modes.

entries.tell: More than one accent colour, or warm and cool greys mixed on one page.
entries.prompt: Does one accent carry every action and every highlight, and do all greys lean the same way?
entries.instead: Keep one accent for actions, tint every neutral toward one temperature, and use semantic colours only for state.

entries.tell: Grey body text laid over a coloured surface.
entries.prompt: Is each text colour on a coloured surface a shade of that surface or a defined on-colour token?
entries.instead: Use the on-colour token the surface defines, and check it against the surface as a pair.

entries.tell: Tinted near-black, noise or grain added as the cure for a flat dark theme.
entries.prompt: Does the dark theme get its depth from layered surfaces and a clear text ladder, not from an overlay?
entries.instead: Define surface steps and a text ladder for dark mode as tokens, and judge them by contrast and hierarchy.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: A default generator typeface that the system does not name. The library bans no other font by name, and a system or workhorse face is fine in operate mode.
entries.instead: Give each typeface a role (display, body, mono) and take it from the system's font tokens.

entries.tell: An oversized italic serif headline over a sans body.
entries.instead: Set the display face to match the system's type roles, and use italics only where the text is stressed.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: Display text with crushed letter-spacing.
entries.instead: Take tracking from the type scale tokens and keep headings readable at their smallest size.

entries.tell: Heading levels that resolve to nearly the same size.
entries.instead: Make each heading level visibly smaller than the one above, using the type scale.

entries.tell: A small caps kicker above the heading of most sections.
entries.instead: Open a section with its heading, and keep a kicker for the one place where it names a real category.

entries.tell: One word of a headline set in an accent colour or italic.
entries.prompt: Does the headline read as one clear statement without a highlighted word?
entries.instead: Write the headline so it holds on its own, and spend emphasis in one deliberate place on the page.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: A monospace face used on labels and headings only to look technical.
entries.prompt: Does every monospace use show code, data, a shortcut or an identifier?
entries.instead: Reserve the mono role for text that is literally code or data, and set labels in the body face.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: Geist, Outfit or Satoshi picked as the fresh alternative to the usual defaults.
entries.prompt: Was the typeface chosen for this product's voice and written down with its role, or only to dodge a default?
entries.instead: Choose from the brand and the content, and state why in the type section of the design file.

entries.tell: Bordered or shadowed surfaces placed inside other cards.
entries.instead: Use one surface level for grouping, and separate inner items with spacing or a divider.

entries.tell: One corner radius on every element.
entries.instead: Pick radii from a short ladder and tie each step to a component class.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: One gap value used between everything.
entries.instead: Use the spacing steps to separate section, group and item, so spacing shows the structure.

entries.tell: The same icon, heading and text shape stamped across most sections.
entries.instead: Shape each section from its content, and give one section the signature treatment.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: A faint grid-line pattern behind page content.
entries.instead: Leave the background flat, or use a pattern only on a real canvas or map surface.

entries.tell: Three equal cards in a row as the default section.
entries.prompt: Does each section's layout follow from its content, or is it the three-card default?
entries.instead: Let the content's shape pick the layout, and give one section the signature treatment.

entries.tell: A hero built from a big number, a small label and a gradient accent.
entries.prompt: Is every figure in the hero real, sourced and tied to the page's one claim?
entries.instead: Lead with the product's own claim or a real screenshot, and show a number only when it is true and sourced.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: Every block centred, with the same stack of heading, line and two buttons.
entries.prompt: Does the alignment of each section come from how it is read, or from habit?
entries.instead: Align text to the reading edge, and centre only short, standalone statements.

entries.tell: A thick coloured bar down one side of a card.
entries.instead: Show importance with position, size or a label, and keep card edges plain.

entries.tell: A heavy accent border around a rounded card.
entries.instead: Frame content with one quiet border token, and leave the accent for the action.

entries.tell: A hairline border together with a wide soft shadow on one surface.
entries.instead: Choose one depth cue per surface, a border or a shadow, from the elevation tokens.

entries.tell: A row of coloured dots that carries no state.
entries.instead: Show a dot only when it maps to a real state, and pair it with a text label.

entries.tell: A repeating stripe texture used as surface filler.
entries.instead: Keep surfaces flat, or define a texture token with a stated purpose.

entries.tell: Components shown only in their default state.
entries.prompt: Does every interactive component define hover, focus, disabled, loading, empty and error?
entries.instead: Specify each state in the component contract and build the states with the component.

entries.tell: A modal dialog for a task that does not need to interrupt.
entries.prompt: Would the task work inline, in a popover or on its own page?
entries.instead: Keep the user in context with an inline or popover pattern, and reserve the modal for a decision that blocks.

entries.tell: One filled and one ghost button on every call to action.
entries.prompt: Does each action group show one primary action that matches the page's goal?
entries.instead: Give the page one primary action, and make secondary actions plain links or quiet buttons.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: Emoji used as icons, bullets or section markers.
entries.instead: Use one icon set at one stroke weight, or use plain text labels.

entries.tell: An image with an empty, missing or placeholder source.
entries.instead: Ship real images with set width and height, or design an empty state with a real component.

entries.tell: A rocket for launch, a shield for security, a bulb for ideas.
entries.prompt: Does each icon say something specific about this product's feature?
entries.instead: Draw or choose an icon from the product's own objects and actions.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: Icons from several sets or with different stroke weights on one page.
entries.prompt: Do all icons share one set, size scale and stroke weight?
entries.instead: Standardise on one icon set and record its size and stroke in the design file.

entries.tell: A hero illustration assembled from basic shapes.
entries.prompt: Is the image authored artwork, a real screenshot or a photo of the subject?
entries.instead: Use real product views or authored artwork, and leave the space empty when there is none.

entries.tell: Transitions that animate every property.
entries.instead: Name the properties, and animate only transform and opacity.

entries.tell: Transitions on properties other than transform, opacity and their relatives.
entries.instead: Move things with transform and fade them with opacity.

entries.tell: Animation with no prefers-reduced-motion handling.
entries.instead: Add a reduced-motion block that stops the motion or shortens it to a fade.

entries.tell: Animating width, height, margin, padding or position.
entries.instead: Animate transform for movement, and open a disclosure once with a single short transition.

entries.tell: Bounce or overshoot easing on entrances.
entries.instead: Use a short ease-out curve at 150 to 300 milliseconds and keep one curve across the system.

entries.tell: A pulsing dot that implies live activity.
entries.instead: Animate a dot only when it is bound to live data, and show the real value beside it.

entries.tell: Auto-scrolling strips of logos, words or cards.
entries.instead: Lay the items out in a static row or grid the reader can scan at their own pace.

entries.tell: Images or cards that zoom or rotate on hover.
entries.instead: Show hover with a colour or underline change, and leave images still.

entries.tell: Bouncing chevrons or scroll to explore labels.
entries.instead: Let the next section's top edge show above the fold so the page invites scrolling.

entries.tell: The same fade and slide on every section as it enters.
entries.prompt: Does each motion explain a change of state, or only decorate the entrance?
entries.instead: Animate only state changes, and let everything else appear at rest.

entries.tell: Em dashes chained through paragraphs and headings.
entries.instead: Write short sentences and use a comma, a colon or a full stop.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: Filler verbs such as elevate, seamless and supercharge.
entries.instead: Name what the product does with a concrete verb and an object.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: Slogans in the shape "Not an X. A Y."
entries.instead: State the claim once, in a plain sentence with a specific noun.

sources.name: Capital and Compute, fix AI slop tell by tell

entries.tell: Placeholder people such as John Doe in quotes and avatars.
entries.instead: Use real, attributed people, or leave the section out.

entries.tell: Made-up metrics, user counts and logo walls.
entries.instead: State only figures you can source, and link the source.

entries.tell: Several buttons in one viewport that ask for the same action.
entries.instead: Show one primary action per viewport and word it as the outcome.

entries.tell: Numbered section labels where nothing is a sequence.
entries.instead: Number sections only when the order matters, such as steps.

entries.tell: Chains of middle dots between short words.
entries.instead: Separate items with a comma or list them, and keep one dot for a real byline.

entries.tell: Title Case on headings, buttons and labels. The library chose sentence case, against the Title Case that one source asks for.
entries.prompt: Are all headings, buttons and labels in sentence case, with proper nouns capitalised?
entries.instead: Write interface text in sentence case and capitalise only the first word and proper nouns.

entries.tell: A button labelled Submit, OK or Click here.
entries.prompt: Does each button name the result of pressing it?
entries.instead: Label the button with the verb and object, such as Save changes.

entries.tell: An error that says Oops, or a success message with an exclamation mark.
entries.prompt: Does each error say what happened and what to do next, in a calm voice?
entries.instead: Write the cause and the next step in plain words, next to the field it concerns.
